title: Tool handshake protocol and backwards negotiation for OpenAI-style tools vs legacy functions
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design and implement a lightweight handshake protocol layered on top of the existing runtime request path to negotiate tool/function calling semantics between OpenAI-style tool requests and our legacy function-invocation surface. Goal: enable progressive rollouts, streamed tool responses with preserved provenance, and minimal changes to customer SDKs while ensuring deterministic fallbacks for older clients.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes a 3-way handshake for tool calls: client declares tool-mode version, server advertises supported compatibility flags, negotiation selects an invocation envelope
Streaming tool output includes standardized chunk metadata (e.g., tool_call.start, tool_call.chunk, tool_call.end) and can be consumed by both new SDKs and legacy function handlers
Legacy function names are mapped to canonical tool IDs with a prioritized fallback list preserved in request metadata
No customer-facing breaking changes for clients that do not opt into the new handshake; canary rollout path verified on Dedicated staging
Automated integration tests covering name collisions, missing args, and partial streaming failures added to runtime test-suite
comments: 2025-02-15 - Ava Martinez: Created ticket after RFC sync. Problem: inconsistent naming and payload shapes between 'functions' (legacy) and 'tools' (OpenAI style) cause runtime routing ambiguity and loss of invocation provenance in streaming responses.

2025-02-16 - Liam Chen: Spike complete. Implemented a prototype handshake that adds a small 'compat' negotiation header and preserves original invocation payload under metadata.__orig_call. Prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321

2025-02-17 - Design review (Elena Park): Suggested including a human-readable 'confidence' hint in the negotiated envelope to help Console interpret ambiguous mappings. Added to AC as optional metadata.

2025-02-18 - Security review request (Ravi Patel): Marked for security review due to metadata preservation of customer payloads. Will add KMS tagging for any persisted mapping tables. Action: follow-up task to add retention/rotation policy.

2025-02-19 - QA (Sofia Morales): Integration tests for stream chunk ordering and reconnect semantics queued. Found race where a fallback mapping applied after stream start causes duplicate tool invocations; mitigation: atomic mapping decision prior to emitting tool_call.start chunk.

2025-02-20 - Liam Chen: Implementing canonical-tool-id registry (in-memory + persisted seed) and wire format v0.2. Preparing canary patch for Dedicated staging. Linked confluence: https://redwood-inference.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/Tool+Handshake+Protocol
notes: - Option A: embed full legacy payload under metadata.__orig_call (easy rollback, small size overhead).
- Option B: transform legacy payload to canonical schema at ingress (faster runtime path, higher risk for rollbacks).
Decision: go with Option A for initial rollout to minimize blast radius; Option B remains a future optimization for high-throughput Dedicated customers.
- Use chunk metadata types: tool_call.start (includes negotiated_tool_id, canonical_schema_version), tool_call.chunk (seq, partial_output), tool_call.end (final_status, provenance_token).
- Ensure that when a legacy consumer receives a stream it can reassemble and map canonical_tool_id -> legacy_name using the preserved fallback list in metadata.
- Maintain a prioritized mapping table: [canonical_tool_id -> ordered list of legacy aliases]. Mapping table seeded from model onboarding data and customer-provided aliases.
- Add metrics: handshake_success_rate, handshake_fallback_rate, stream_reconnect_rate_by_tool, duplicate_invocation_count.
- Add a console flag to visualize negotiated envelope and original payload for debugging (redact PII by default).
